Emission of Unregulated Pollutants
Federal Energy Administration (FEA). FEA stated that the draft EIS mentioned the possibility of increased sulphate emissions from the use of more and larger catalysts.

They stated that an even more important consideration may be the increased emissions of unregulated pollutants (e.g., particulates) due to recalibration of engines or substitution of diesel engines. As the fuel economy standards are applied to more vehicles, this could become an important problem and close coordination between DOT and EPA will be required on this and the above issue.
Ford Motor Company. Ford claims that particulate matter (smoke) emissions from diesels in known to increase significantly at NOx standards below 1.5 grams per mile. They also point out that although smoke increase may not be an important environmental factor at 1979 NOx levels (2.3 Federal, 2.0 California), the longer term effect must be considered in evaluating the possible substitution of diesel for gasoline engines.
<u>Summary</u>. FEA and Ford claim that the introduction of diesels will result in more particulate emission. FEA makes the same claim for the recalibration of engines to meet an AFES.
